newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha firms on good transatlantic demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha firms on good transatlantic demand.

text.p: NWE naphtha held a firm tone on Wednesday with transatlantic demand the main engine.
"The big motor is the U.S.," said one trader. A number of market players were also taking comfort from a belief that petrochemical demand would kick in during the second half of the month.
A full range parcel, estimated at 5-10,000 tonnes, was sold at a p&c rate. Traders said the material was likely to be used to build a transatlantic cargo.
Physical cif NWE cargoes were pegged $1-2 above swaps which were heard at $230-231 for Jan and $227-228 for Feb.

Freight costs remain high from Europe to the Americas, but this has not stopped material heading transatlantic. Traders said 100,000 tonnes is loading from North Africa for Brazil at the weekend and next week.
Some traders felt high transatlantic freight rates and limited European interest would limit price gains.
"An upward move unlikely unless Brent goes up," said one trader.
